result:
Since nothing is built yet, I'll stage this from the outcomes rather than from a gap table. Nothing in `specs/` is a spec or a roadmap: you have a research brief and three research reports. The outcomes below are therefore candidates I drew from those files. Each one is marked with its source, and you confirm or cut it.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size at each of the four stages (1→2, 2→3, 3→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back) for total nonfarm, over the full history | prompt Part A; chatgpt §1.2 | Small data: one SA and one NSA series, with a few hundred monthly vintages. The FRED/ALFRED API allows 120 requests a minute. The earliest usable vintage date is unconfirmed. |
| O2 | O1 broken out by NAICS supersector | prompt Part C (hierarchy) | **Unknown.** Supersector vintage coverage on ALFRED is unconfirmed. If it is thin, filling it from archived releases costs your time. |
| O3 | SA one- and two-month revisions split into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part | prompt Driver 1; all three reports call it unstudied | Data comes with O1/O2. The method is open, so the core stage measures the cost. |
| O4 | How collection days and first-closing rate relate to one-month revision spread | prompt Driver 2; claude §1 | Collection days are arithmetic on the release calendar. How far back the published collection-rate series goes is unconfirmed. |
| O5 | Annual series of BLS operating capacity: real appropriations, CRs/shutdowns/sequestration, FTE, sample size, with sources | prompt Drivers 3–5, Part B | Mostly your time: about 40 annual points per series, transcribed by hand from budget justifications and FedScope. Hours, not compute. |
| O6 | The multi-vintage Bayesian model: latent truth, news and noise by stage, covariates on log-scale with SV, Student-t errors, benchmark as an irregular observation with wedge-back, supersector pooling, structural-change handling | prompt Part C | **Compute unknown until a fit runs.** Rough scale: ~500 months × 4 stages × 2 (NSA/SA) × ~11 supersectors under NUTS. |
| O7 | Evidence on whether covariate-driven scale beats a constant-variance baseline: dispersion-targeted predictive checks, LOO, pseudo-real-time | prompt Part C (validation) | LOO comes almost free from one fit. Pseudo-real-time costs one refit per forecast origin, each at O6's fit time. |

The three research reports already deliver the literature review and gap analysis (Parts A–B), so I've left those out as outcomes.

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision record (O1, O2). Known progression:** total nonfarm first, then supersectors. Every other track reads this data. That makes A a dependency of the others, not a reason to merge them.
- **B: Seasonal vs. sample (O3). Research.** Split from C because either answer stands without the other.
- **C: Collection interval (O4). Research.** This is the sharpest within-year variation and the best-identified driver. Joined to D, it would wait on the full model.
- **D: Capacity and the full model (O5, O6, O7). Research.** The capacity covariates are slow and collinear, and only the full model can address them honestly. It is the most expensive track and the most open one.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14, with uv, pytest and ruff (repo). One risk to check: JAX may not have Python 3.14 wheels yet.
- Stack: NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax if needed, ArviZ, Polars (prompt).
- The estimand is revision **scale**, so covariates enter the variance, not only the mean (prompt).

**Proposed name:** `ces-revisions`, written to `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists yet.

## What I need from you

**Please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks against each other, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name.**

Two optional ways to firm up the "unknown" cost notes before I write the roadmap:

- I can read the data-inventory sections of the three reports (chatgpt §3.3, gemini "Data Availability Inventory"). So far I've read only their first 3,000 characters.
- I can run one probe: list the ALFRED vintages for the total nonfarm SA and NSA series and for one supersector series.

Say yes to either along with your ranking.
